target: Il est essentiel que chacun fasse sa part.
english: It's essential that everyone does their part.
tip: 'Il est essentiel que' + subjunctive. Judgments of necessity trigger the subjunctive mood.

target: L'auteur dont j'ai lu tous les livres vient de publier un nouveau roman.
english: The author whose books I've read has just published a new novel.
tip: 'dont' bundles in the 'of whom/whose': 'l'auteur dont j'ai lu tous les livres' = the author of whom I've read all the books.

target: Allons-y, il est déjà tard.
english: Let's go, it's already late.
tip: Allons-y literally means 'let's go there' – that little y stands in for a place English just leaves out.

target: Regardez cette vue magnifique !
english: Look at this magnificent view!
tip: Regarder already means 'look at' – there's no word for 'at'. You look the view directly: regardez cette vue.

target: Je doute qu'il vienne ce soir.
english: I doubt he'll come tonight.
tip: Doubt undercuts certainty, so French flips to the subjunctive: 'je doute qu'il vienne', not 'vient' – the same switch you get after 'ne pas penser que'.

target: Ne te lève pas, reste assis.
english: Don't get up, stay seated.
tip: In a positive command the pronoun follows (lève-toi), but negate it and te jumps back in front: ne te lève pas.

target: Appelle-moi dès que tu arrives !
english: Call me as soon as you arrive!
tip: Positive imperative with pronoun: verb-moi. Appelle-moi (hyphen required).

target: Prépare-toi, nous partons dans dix minutes.
english: Get ready, we're leaving in ten minutes.
tip: dans dix minutes = in ten minutes from now. Use dans, not en – en dix minutes would mean it takes ten minutes.

target: Dépêche-toi, on va être en retard !
english: Hurry up, we're going to be late!
tip: In 'Dépêche-toi, on va être en retard', on means 'we' – but the verb keeps its he/she form: on va, not on allons.

target: Tu devrais appeler ta mère plus souvent.
english: You should call your mother more often.
tip: devrais is the conditional of devoir and means 'should', not 'must' – it's softer advice: tu devrais appeler.

target: Il est possible que nous déménagions l'année prochaine.
english: It's possible we'll move next year.
tip: "Il est possible que" expresses uncertainty and triggers the subjunctive.

target: Choisis ce qui te plaît sur le menu.
english: Choose what you like on the menu.
tip: plaire flips the subject and object: te plaît turns 'what you like' into 'what pleases you' – you're the receiver: ce qui te plaît.

target: Lave-toi les mains avant de passer à table.
english: Wash your hands before sitting down to eat.
tip: French says les mains, not 'your hands' – with body parts you use the reflexive plus 'the': lave-toi les mains.

target: Si j'avais su, je ne serais pas venu.
english: If I had known, I wouldn't have come.
tip: To rewind and imagine a different past, pair 'si' + the had-form with a would-have clause: 'si j'avais su, je ne serais pas venu' = had I known, I wouldn't have come.

target: Je boirais bien un thé après le dîner.
english: I could really go for a tea after dinner.
tip: boirais is 'would drink', but add bien and it means 'I could really go for one': je boirais bien un thé.

target: Si on commençait maintenant, on finirait avant midi.
english: If we started now, we would finish before noon.
tip: After si you never use the conditional. Si takes the imperfect (commençait); the 'would' half gets it: on finirait.

target: Le marché où j'achète mes légumes est ouvert le samedi.
english: The market where I buy my vegetables is open on Saturdays.
tip: le samedi doesn't mean one Saturday – with the article it means 'on Saturdays', every week: ouvert le samedi.

target: C'est le livre dont tout le monde parle en ce moment.
english: It's the book everyone is talking about right now.
tip: You say parler de quelque chose, so 'the book everyone talks about' needs dont, the word that swallows that de.

target: Elle avait déjà quitté la maison quand le téléphone a sonné.
english: She had already left the house when the phone rang.
tip: avait quitté = 'had left'. For the earlier of two past events French uses this past-of-the-past, before plain a sonné.

target: Bien qu'il pleuve, nous allons sortir.
english: Although it's raining, we're going out.
tip: "Bien que" (although) always requires the subjunctive.

target: J'aimerais apprendre à jouer du piano.
english: I would like to learn to play the piano.
tip: You play du piano, not 'le' piano – instruments take jouer de, while sports take jouer à: jouer au foot.

target: Je suis déçu que le concert soit annulé.
english: I'm disappointed the concert is cancelled.
tip: Adjectives of emotion + que trigger the subjunctive: soit, not est.

target: Tu devrais lire ce livre, il est passionnant.
english: You should read this book, it's fascinating.
tip: 'devoir' in the conditional turns 'must' into gentle advice: 'tu devrais lire' = you should read, softer than 'tu dois' = you have to.

target: Il est dommage que nous ne puissions pas rester.
english: It's a shame we can't stay.
tip: "Puissions" is the subjunctive of pouvoir. "Il est dommage que" expresses regret.

target: C'est la plus belle ville que j'aie jamais visitée.
english: It's the most beautiful city I've ever visited.
tip: A superlative claim tips the que-clause into the subjunctive: 'la plus belle ville que j'aie jamais visitée' uses 'aie', not 'ai'.

target: Je te prête mon vélo pourvu que tu fasses attention.
english: I'll lend you my bike provided you're careful.
tip: "Pourvu que" (provided that) triggers the subjunctive.

target: Avant que tu ne t'en ailles, j'ai quelque chose à te dire.
english: Before you leave, I have something to tell you.
tip: In formal French, an expletive "ne" can appear after "avant que" without negative meaning.

target: Elle exige que les employés soient ponctuels.
english: She demands that the employees be punctual.
tip: "Exiger que" (to demand that) triggers the subjunctive.

target: Partageons le gâteau équitablement.
english: Let's share the cake fairly.
tip: There's no word for 'let's' in French – the -ons ending carries it. Partageons = 'let's share'. Any nous-form verb becomes a suggestion this way.

target: Explique-lui la situation calmement.
english: Explain the situation to him calmly.
tip: In a positive command the pronoun hops behind the verb, joined by a hyphen: 'explique-lui' – but negate it and the pronoun jumps back in front: 'ne lui explique pas'.
